pr_title: bluetooth: host: Add APIs to track Unenhanced ATT MTU
pr_body:
### Description
This PR features an additional API to get the current UATT MTU and a callback on UATT MTU changes. This in order to provide the ability to keep track of this parameter, regardless of the presence of additional EATT channels.

Fixes #68070.

### Changes
- Add `uatt_mtu_updated` to get notified on UATT MTU changes on a given connection.
- Add `bt_gatt_get_uatt_mtu` to get a connection's current UATT MTU.
- Update MTU Update sample to use the above.
- Refactor Babblesim test: MTU Update to have peripheral and central be two separate builds.

### Testing
- Compiled all BabbleSim Testsuite. Ran Bluetooth Host Testsuite locally.
- Built MTU Update Peripheral Sample.
pr_comments:
@alwa-nordic @jori-nordic @Thalley @carlescufi @jhedberg I'd like your inputs on this approach before going any further.

This solution seems the simplest one without:
- Breaking existing code that is relying on `att_mtu_updated`.
- Depending on the BT Stack refactoring involving inclusion of L2CAP channels in the API parameters (#68107).

I know there were mixed feelings on naming it "UATT". That is also up for discussion, provided the approach is OK.

Before taking this PR out of draft state, I'm planning to add Babblesim tests and/or samples supporting this feature (similar to #67858).
A new callback is fine by me.

The spec defines the ATT MTU of a bearer as a single value that's the same for rx and tx. See `bt_att_mtu`. I think it may be best to give this value in the callback to minimize user errors.

We may need to specify more precisely what the values in the callback mean, so that the behavior does not change with implementation details. Maybe like it's the value of the "Client Rx MTU" and the "Server Rx MTU" fields in the MTU exchange PDU, where the locally controlled value is `rx`?

The only use I can think of for separate rx and tx MTU is to allow the application to detect that the local side is the bottleneck, which is useful, but then maybe we should instead give the application the final ATT MTU and the remote mtu. Can you think of other use cases?

Bluetooth WG:

- Remove rx and tx and instead use att_mtu
- Add the missing `bt_uatt_get_mtu` getter
- This is a short-term solution. The long-term one is to replace `bt_conn` with `bt_l2cap_chan` in all ATT/GATT calls.

> Bluetooth WG:
> 
> * Remove rx and tx and instead use att_mtu
> * Add the missing `bt_uatt_get_mtu` getter
> * This is a short-term solution. The long-term one is to replace `bt_conn` with `bt_l2cap_chan` in all ATT/GATT calls.

I've addressed the agreed changes. PR is up for review now.

Should the new API be labeled experimental?

Also, we should take a moment to discover and discuss in detail the exact behavior of this new API, so that we are sure we know what we are making.

I have some observations which I think are worth discussing:

 - `uatt_mtu_updated` will always fire at connection establishment with the value `23`.
 - `uatt_mtu_updated` will always fire after a exchange even if the value does not change.
 - There can be two exchanges, and `uatt_mtu_updated` will fire for each, even though the value will be the same.
 - It's not possible to deduce whether the MTU exhange has happened using `bt_att_get_uatt_mtu`.
 - The exchange can happen at almost any moment, so the value of `bt_att_get_uatt_mtu` can be stale.

I'll withhold my comments about alternatives for a moment, so we can all consider it for ourselves.

When we are happy with the behavior, etc, we should document it all, and ideally test it too.

@alwa-nordic thanks for your feedback!

> Should the new API be labeled experimental?

Yes. I'm not familiar with the process, though.
https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/develop/api/api_lifecycle.html#experimental mentions marking the API header with a versioning scheme, but I'm failing to find an instance doing it so. May I get some guidance?

> I have some observations which I think are worth discussing:
> 
> uatt_mtu_updated will always fire at connection establishment with the value 23.
> uatt_mtu_updated will always fire after a exchange even if the value does not change.
> There can be two exchanges, and uatt_mtu_updated will fire for each, even though the value will be the same.
> It's not possible to deduce whether the MTU exhange has happened using bt_att_get_uatt_mtu.
> The exchange can happen at almost any moment, so the value of bt_att_get_uatt_mtu can be stale.
> I'll withhold my comments about alternatives for a moment, so we can all consider it for ourselves.
> 
> When we are happy with the behavior, etc, we should document it all, and ideally test it too.

Sounds like the introduction of the UATT MTU callback may require additional req's definition (reminds me of #64172). Would it be OK to drop the callback from this PR: only merge the getter API (which is what's requested originally on #68070) and then handle the async callback on a separate PR where we define the expected behavior and properly test it?

More context to think about:

A function to get the current ATT_MTU is not useful (by itself) to determine where to truncate a notification because the ATT_MTU could change before the notification is sent, and whether the ATT PDU maxes out the ATT_MTU is relevant to the protocol:

Core 3.F.3.4.7.1 "ATT_HANDLE_VALUE_NTF":
> If the attribute value is longer than (ATT_MTU-3) octets, then only the first (ATT_MTU-3) octets of this attributes value can be sent in a notification.
>
> Note: For a client to get a long attribute, it must use the ATT_READ_BLOB_REQ PDU (see Section 3.4.4.5) following the receipt of this notification

I've updated the PR based on the latest feedback:
- Dropped Callback API.
- Brought back `compile.sh` script and tested it's working.
- Modified Getter API docstring to incorporate suggestions.
- Updated Doc Release notes to mark the getter API as experimental.
- Changed assert in code for k_oops, per suggestion.

LMK if you have further comments!
There are some conflicts. I'll need to rebase

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Host: missing api: bt_uatt_get_mtu
issue_context.body:
As a Bluetooth LE Audio subsystem developer, I need my API to enforce a requirement from the specification: Some audio functions require the UATT MTU to be at least 64. They must return an error otherwise.

Currently, there is no way to get the UATT MTU (in a reliable way) from the Host.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A new API: `uint16_t bt_uatt_get_mtu(struct bt_conn *conn)`

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Not enforcing the ATT MTU at service level. This could cause hard-to-debug errors for the user.

**Why the current API does not satisfy my requirements**
 - `bt_gatt_get_mtu`: Affected by EATT MTU. I need the UATT MTU.
 - `bt_gatt_exchange_mtu`: The service layer is not the place to initiate the MTU exchange. That is done by the sample/application.
 - `bt_gatt_cb.att_mtu_updated`: Affected by EATT MTU. I need the UATT MTU.
comments: @alwa-nordic is this issue up for grabs? I could tackle it as it would enable me coming up with a solution for #72018.
Yes, issue is up for grabs. Thanks for taking it! :)
Sorry for the delay. Picking up this now.
